description: CBOR conformance vector provenance (testing-strategy spec requirement 'Conformance vector provenance'). Every vector file under spec-derived/ and constructed/ is labeled with its source kind and provenance. Vectors are NEVER captured from third-party authenticators (cleanroom rule): spec-derived vectors are transcribed from the CTAP2.1 specification's own published examples, constructed vectors are generated by the deterministic seeded generator (crates/fidoh-transport-soft/examples/generate_vectors.rs) and must regenerate byte-identically (CI: .github/workflows/vectors.yml).
spec_reference: FIDO Client to Authenticator Protocol (CTAP) 2.1, Proposed Standard, June 15, 2021 (https://fidoalliance.org/specs/fido-v2.1-ps-20210615/fido-client-to-authenticator-protocol-v2.1-ps-20210615.html)
note_on_sections: CTAP2.1 section 6 (Authenticator API) defines the command/response structures in tables and diagnostic CBOR notation only; it publishes no wire-format byte examples. The byte-string examples the spec does publish live in section 10.2, section 10.3, and section 11.3.6; the getInfo response example in section 12.5 ('Sample CTAP2 authenticatorGetInfo response (CBOR)') is a two-member fragment printed in diagnostic notation, not a byte string. Vectors below are therefore transcribed from the sections that actually carry bytes, and from section 10.3's mapped CTAP2 structures serialized per the spec's own section 8 canonical rules; per-file provenance cites the exact source.

constructed.seed_note: 0xC0FFEE00; matches SEED in the generator source. Re-running the generator reproduces these files byte-identically.

provenance.note: Snapshot of one resident example.com credential minted under the fixed seeded RNG; regenerate with the generator and diff (CI asserts byte-identical).

Snapshot of three resident example.com credentials plus one other.example credential, initial_sign_count 7, minted under the fixed seeded RNG; regenerate with the generator and diff (CI asserts byte-identical).

provenance.spec_section: CTAP2.1 section 11.3.6 (Fragmentation), example 'Sample authenticatorMakeCredential request using short APDU encoding and chaining mode'
provenance.transcription: Faithful transcription of the 263-byte string in the spec's code block (one CTAP command byte 0x01 followed by the canonical-CBOR makeCredential request map). Verbatim from the published example; no re-encoding applied.
provenance.framing: leading CTAP command byte 0x01; CBOR payload starts at offset 1

provenance.spec_section: CTAP2.1 section 11.3.6 (Fragmentation), authenticator responses to APDU commands 2-4 of the same example, reassembled
provenance.transcription: The example's fragmented response, concatenated exactly as the example specifies (response payload bytes of the three APDU exchanges; per-exchange status/trailer words 6100/61A7/9000 stripped per the example's own fragmentation semantics). Result: one 0x00 status byte followed by the 674-byte canonical-CBOR authenticatorMakeCredential response map (fmt, authData, attStmt with alg/sig/x5c). All bytes verbatim from the published example; only the fragmentation-chosen split points are unwound, no byte is altered.
provenance.framing: leading response status byte 0x00; CBOR payload starts at offset 1

provenance.spec_section: CTAP2.1 section 10.3 (Using the authenticatorGetAssertion Command with CTAP1/U2F authenticators), 'Sample CTAP2 authenticatorGetAssertion Request (CBOR)'
provenance.transcription: The example's CBOR map {1: rpId "example.com", 2: clientDataHash, 3: [{type, id}], 5: {up: true}} serialized per CTAP2.1 section 8 canonical rules. Member values (rpId string, clientDataHash h'6871...F141', credential id h'3EBD...0038') are transcribed verbatim from the example; the spec prints this structure in diagnostic notation only, so the canonical byte serialization is derived from the spec's own section 8 encoding rules (integer/length minimality, len-first map-key order, definite lengths).
provenance.framing: no framing byte: raw CBOR command map

provenance.transcription: The example's mapped response map {1: credential descriptor, 2: authenticatorData, 3: signature} serialized per CTAP2.1 section 8 canonical rules. The descriptor id and the byte strings h'A379...1947 010000003B' (authData) and h'3044...858E' (signature) are transcribed verbatim from the example; byte serialization derived from the spec's own section 8 canonical rules (diagnostic notation only in the spec).
provenance.framing: no framing byte: raw CBOR response map

not_found.getinfo_response: CTAP2.1 section 6.4 (authenticatorGetInfo) publishes NO request or response byte-string example; section 6 as a whole contains zero wire examples, and the section 12.5 getInfo sample is a partial fragment ({1: ["FIDO_2_0"], 2: ["hmac-secret"], ...}) in diagnostic notation, not transcribable to ground-truth bytes. A getInfo vector is therefore NOT included rather than fabricated; the constructed tier's snapshot vectors and the existing unit tests cover the getInfo shape.
